VBO:0200342.summary: The Chilean Terrier is described by its national standard as lively, alert and responsive, with reserve toward strangers. Its small-game and farm work included catching rodents. When rural families moved into towns in the late nineteenth century, they brought these dogs along to hunt rats around factories and shared housing.
VBO:0200342.shortDescription: A lively, alert Chilean farm terrier with a rat-catching tradition and a reserved response to strangers.

sources.title: Kennel Club de Chile — official Chilean Terrier standard, effective 2July2020
sources.evidence: Entire actual standard read. Official effective date 02July2020, not2024 filename date. Normative docile, alert, vivacious, reserved with strangers. Small-game/farm/companion purposes and history of late19th-century rural families bringing dogs to urban ratting contexts directly stated. Literal adult near-square males/slightly longer females, 45:55 chest:leg proportions, short firm nearly straight back, high withers, moderate chest/tuck, triangular head/muzzle slightly shorter than skull, small folded high V ears and short tight harsh coat. White entire body/neck/tail with black-and-tan head selected. Full natural low-inserted tail no longer than hock carried high with slight/sickle curve, NEVER curled over back. Natural bobtails permitted but not selected. No health, climate guarantee, child safety, pedigree, ancestry certainty or international recognition claims transferred.
